text: Mobile app development begins with understanding your target users and their devices. One of the first decisions is choosing between native and cross-platform development. Native apps are built specifically for iOS or Android, offering better performance and access to device features, but they require separate codebases. Cross-platform tools like Flutter or React Native let you write one codebase for both systems, saving time and money, though performance may slightly suffer. Regardless of the approach, responsive design is essential—your app must adapt smoothly to different screen sizes and orientations. After development, you publish through app stores like Google Play or the App Store, which have strict review processes. Finally, performance matters: users expect fast loading times, smooth animations, and minimal battery drain. A poorly performing app, no matter how beautiful, will quickly be deleted.
